verdict.rationale: 2FAS Auth documents encrypted sync to the user's own iCloud or Google Drive, plus export files, explicitly to protect tokens if the phone is damaged or lost. Its docs also state that service keys can be recovered after losing the device, and backups can be password-encrypted. 2FAS Pass separately documents a recovery page and a Decryption Kit for restoring the vault on a different device. Missing for 10: step-by-step first-party restore instructions specific to Auth tokens on a new device, and independent or hands-on corroboration that the restore works.

support.subject: As an everyday user, losing my phone doesn't lose my accounts — a documented recovery path restores my tokens on a new device

citations.quote: You can enable secure data syncing with your personal iCloud or Google Drive to protect yourself from losing Tokens in case of phone damage or loss.
Even if you lose your mobile device, you can recover service keys because they are stored in a secure cloud backup.
Synchronize your Tokens with 2FAS export files, iCloud or Google Drive.
Learn how to restore access to your 2FAS Pass Vault or run it on a different device.
